transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-09
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jesse (Redwood AE), Marisol (Redwood SE), Omar (Redwood SE), Priya (BlueHarbor VP Platform), Liam (BlueHarbor SRE), Sara (BlueHarbor Security), Daniel (BlueHarbor ML)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping to define success criteria, reserved GPU sizing, burst strategy, fallback rules and an initial benchmark plan. Goal: 4–6 week pilot, prove p95 latency under 300ms for 512-token gen at peak, and show cost delta between reserved vs hosted burst.

Topics:
- Workload characterization and peak QPS
- Reserved capacity recommendation and burst plan
- Fallback sequencing (model variants, regions, capacity tiers)
- Benchmarks: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, tail lat and cost per 1M tokens
- Timeline and next steps

Action items (high level): Jesse to send runbook + pricing, Daniel to provide traces, Redwood to propose benchmark harness and initial config.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jesse (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanna make this real tight, uh Priya, Liam, thanks for the time. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Priya (BlueHarbor): Hi yes Priya here, Liam and Sara and Daniel are on as well.
[00:18] Liam (BlueHarbor): morning all, Liam.
[00:22] Jesse: Great. So the goal for this call is to scope the PoC runbook, figure out the reserved GPU sizing and how you want to handle burst and fallbacks. Marisol will jump into perf details.
[00:33] Marisol (Redwood): Cool, I'll start with a few clarifying q's about your traffic. Priya, can you give us the ask — what are your peak qps and typical request types?
[00:44] Priya: Sure. So we run a conversational assistant inside our helpdesk flow. Typical prompt lengths average 80 tokens, generation target normally 250-512 tokens for longer responses, but 90% of calls are under 300 tokens. Peak business hours we see approx 180 rps sustained for 30–45m during a campaign spike; baseline is ~20 rps.
[01:06] Jesse: Great that's helpful. Daniel, do you have the traces available?
[01:10] Daniel (BlueHarbor): We have the last 7 days of traffic; I can upload a trace, albeit scrubbed. It includes timestamps and token counts, but there's some metadata we won't share.
[01:19] Marisol: Perfect — the trace helps us estimate active KV cache hit rates and batching opportunities. For that profile we'd suggest starting the PoC with reserved capacity sized for your steady-state high (say 180 rps concurrency model) then allow burst to double capacity.
[01:33] Liam: Uh quick q — by reserved capacity you mean dedicated GPU pool? What's the minimum? We don't want to overcommit.
[01:40] Omar (Redwood): Right, reserved = dedicated Redwood Dedicated pool. For that workload we recommend starting at 4x A10G-equivalent instances which we've seen handle around 200 rps for 256-token median with continuous batching, but if you want tighter headroom for p95 under 300ms we'd recommend 6x A100-equivalent or 4x A100 depending on quantization.
[01:59] Sara (BlueHarbor): A100s are expensive. Can you quantify the delta vs the 4x A10G option? Cost per hour ballpark?
[02:06] Jesse: Yes we'll include pricing in the runbook. Rough numbers in our catalog: A10G pool runs X/hour, A100 is about 2.8x that. But the key is cost per token — with KV cache and smart batching the 4x A10G option sometimes matches latency for median requests; tail p95 is where A100 helps.
[02:24] Priya: For success criteria we want: p95 under 300ms for 512-token responses during peak, end-to-end SLA of 99.9% for the pilot, and memory/data segregation — we need VPC + customer-managed KMS.
[02:38] Marisol: That's reasonable. For the p95 target we need to define where we're measuring — network + model runtime? We recommend measuring at the API edge (response time seen by your app) and also instrumenting model-side times. That way we can separate infra vs network.
[02:55] Daniel: We'll instrument on our side and provide agent traces.
[02:59] Liam: Regarding burst — what's the burst policy? Can Redwood spin up additional capacity in minutes?
[03:05] Omar: Yes burst is configurable. For Dedicated, burst into a shared burst pool is typically cold start ~30–90s depending on region and GPU type. If you need sub-10s, you need warm standby or additional reserved instances.
[03:18] Priya: So proposal — reserved to cover baseline + 20% headroom, burst to cover up to 2x peak, and fallback policy to degrade gracefully to a smaller model or shorter token length if capacity constrained. Is that doable?
[03:30] Marisol: Absolutely. We usually recommend a three-tier fallback: 1) route to reserved pool; 2) if reserved full, route to a lower-cost compatible variant (quantized or smaller model) in the same region; 3) if region capacity low, fallback to cross-region but only for non-sensitive data. All of this is configurable by policy.
[03:49] Sara: Cross-region raises data residency questions. We need policy that keeps EU customers in EU.
[03:54] Jesse: Agreed — we'll ensure routing policy includes region constraints and data labels. We'll also include audit logging for any cross-region fallbacks.
[04:02] Priya: On the model side, we use an internal distilled model for non-critical responses. Could you support model variants with automatic routing?
[04:08] Marisol: Yes that's a core Redwood capability — model variants, canary routing, and automatic fallback with compatible input/output schemas. Minor gotcha: quantized variants may change output tokenization slightly, so we'll include a quality check step during the pilot.
[04:24] Daniel: Speaking of quality, we need a regression threshold — if output quality drops more than X% on a held-out eval set we want auto-rollbacks.
[04:33] Marisol: We can wire Redwood Optimize eval triggers to monitor BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics or more production-suitable checks (semantic similarity). We'll propose thresholds in the runbook.
[04:45] Liam: For the benchmark itself, what metrics do we need to collect?
[04:48] Omar: At minimum: p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, batching stats, KV cache hit rate, cost per 1M tokens. Also memory metrics and quantization impact.
[05:00] Jesse: We'll provide a benchmark harness that replays your trace with time offsets, plus synthetic spikes. We recommend a 2-hour steady-state run and two 10-minute spike windows to exercise burst/fallback.
[05:13] Priya: Timeline question — how long to get to first benchmark?
[05:16] Jesse: If we get traces by 2026-04-13, Redwood can prepare configs and run a first internal benchmark by 2026-04-20. Customer benchmark window could be scheduled the week of 2026-04-20. That matches the plan in the next steps.
[05:28] Sara: Security — SOC2 and KMS are fine, but we need audit logs and proof around key zeroization on termination. Can you provide SOC2 + KMS docs?
[05:37] Jesse: Yes — we'll attach our SOC 2 type II cert and KMS integration notes. We also provide per-request audit logs and optional HSM integrations for enterprise.
[05:46] Priya: Are you supporting private deployment (VPC) for the pilot or is this hosted? We want to know options.
[05:51] Omar: The pilot can run in Redwood Dedicated within your VPC via our Private control plane — that satisfies VPC + customer KMS. If that's heavy, we can run hosted with strict tenancy and VPC peering for faster time-to-value.
[06:05] Daniel: For the PoC we prefer Private VPC so security can run checks early.
[06:09] Jesse: Noted. We'll include two tracks in the runbook: Private VPC pilot and Hosted fast-track, with estimated setup times (Private ~2–3 weeks to provision network + KMS, Hosted ~2–3 days).
[06:21] Liam: One more operational question — how do we handle KV cache priming? We have many repeated prefixes in chat sessions and hope caching helps.
[06:29] Marisol: Our runtime supports prefix cache priming and auto-KV eviction policies. We'll recommend cache sizes and TTLs based on your trace. Typical improvements for chat flows like yours: 20–40% token cost savings and significant latency drops for warm cache hits.
[06:43] Priya: Great. On success criteria, let's be explicit in the doc: p95 < 300ms for 512-token responses at peak, < 1.2x cost of baseline hosted option for median workload, and functional parity vs our distilled internal model on key evaluation prompts.
[07:00] Marisol: We'll encode those as pass/fail thresholds and include a small test suite of 50 prompts.
[07:07] Jesse: Any blockers from security?
[07:09] Sara: Just we need to review the KMS flow and audit log retention (min 12 months). Also SAML SSO + RBAC requirements for the console.
[07:18] Omar: We'll include RBAC and SSO notes; our enterprise console supports SAML/Okta and fine-grained RBAC. Audit retention can be adjusted per contract.
[07:27] Daniel: For the benchmark harness, can Redwood simulate client-side retries and backpressure? We do exponential backoff in our app.
[07:33] Marisol: Yes the harness supports configurable retry profiles, backpressure, and can replay real inter-arrival times. We'll need the client retry strategy from you.
[07:43] Priya: We'll send a small doc describing request flow, retry policy and which paths are synchronous vs async.
[07:49] Jesse: Cool. Let's walk through a concrete sample PoC run sequence so we all sync on steps.
[07:54] Jesse: Step 0 — customer provides traces and security checklist. Step 1 — Redwood provisions reserved pool + private VPC (if chosen). Step 2 — Redwood runs internal smoke and tuning. Step 3 — joint benchmark window with customer. Step 4 — evaluate metrics vs success criteria and decide on next commit.
[08:11] Priya: Sounds good, can you call out timing for each step?
[08:14] Jesse: Sure: Step 0 (1–3 days to gather traces), Step 1 (2–3 weeks for Private VPC, 2–3 days hosted), Step 2 (~3 days), Step 3 (benchmark week), Step 4 (2–5 days for analysis). Total: Roughly 4–6 weeks end-to-end for Private VPC pilot.
[08:32] Liam: For fallbacks during benchmark we want to see: 1) model variant routing, 2) shorter max tokens, 3) degrade to cached responses for known queries.
[08:42] Marisol: We'll implement all three and show switching latencies. We'll also stress the canary deploys behavior so you can test automatic rollbacks for quality regressions.
[08:53] Priya: Ok. Anything else on benchmarks?
[08:56] Omar: We'll provide a metrics dashboard with per-route p95, GPU util, batch sizes, cache hit rate and estimated cost. We'll also dump raw logs for your SRE to validate.
[09:07] Jesse: Quick clarifying note — the recommended reserved sizing (4 A10G vs 4/6 A100) depends on quantization choices. If you can accept int8 quantized variants, we can get A100-like throughput on A10G in many cases. We'll test both.
[09:24] Daniel: We'll add a note: certain prompts require exact phrasing; quantization shouldn't change answers materially. Quality checks will catch any drift.
[09:31] Priya: Good. Let's recap next steps and owners.
[09:35] Jesse: Recap — Jesse to send the PoC runbook & pricing spreadsheet by Monday (2026-04-12). Daniel to push traces by 2026-04-13. Marisol to deliver benchmark config and proposed metrics by 2026-04-16. Schedule benchmark window week of 2026-04-20. Redwood to attach SOC2 and KMS docs in the runbook.
[09:54] Priya: That works. One ask: can you also include an estimated monthly spend model comparing reserved 4x A10G + burst vs 4x A100 reserved? We want a per-token cost delta.
[10:06] Jesse: Yes — we'll include cost models and a sensitivity analysis for different cache hit rates and batching efficiencies.
[10:15] Sara: Also include SSO/RBAC config sample for our security team to review.
[10:19] Jesse: Noted. Any final Qs?
[10:22] Liam: None from me.
[10:24] Priya: No. Thanks everyone.
[10:26] Jesse: Thanks — we'll follow up with runbook and calendar invite for the benchmark. End.

Post-call notes (auto):
- Redwood to include two pilot tracks (Private VPC vs Hosted) with setup time estimates.
- Add explicit fallback sequence and cross-region rules for sensitive data.
- Benchmark harness to simulate retries/backoff.
- Include cost sensitivity table for token cost vs cache hit rate.
